note: The zones of Riftwalk, one for each collection of the arcade. Each zone is a Gaussian splat world made with Marble by World Labs through the World Labs API on 2026-11-16 (UTC). The splat files in worlds/<zone>/ are Marble's own exports, unchanged. worlds/<zone>/screens.json holds the place of each cabinet screen, found in the world's panorama by games/riftwalk/tools/find-screens.py and placed in the world by games/riftwalk/tools/place-screens.mjs. worlds/<zone>/door.webp is a view into the zone, cut from its panorama by games/riftwalk/tools/door-art.py.

cottage.prompt: A 360 degree view from the exact centre of a dark, crowded, cluttered cyberpunk arcade den with every wall packed with detail at night. Arcade cabinets surround the viewer completely in an unbroken circle: in front, to the left, to the right and behind, twenty-four tall retro cabinets standing shoulder to shoulder, all facing the centre, two metres away. Every cabinet has one large flat upright screen that is switched on and shows only plain bright white light with no picture. The cabinets are glossy black with thick glowing edge strips in warm amber, gold and orange. The room is lit only by neon: the walls and the low ceiling behind the cabinets are covered with glowing neon tubes, neon rings, neon arrows and abstract neon shapes in amber, gold, orange and soft red, with strings of small warm lamps, with tangled hanging cables, pipes, ducts and stacked old monitors showing static between them. Amber and rose haze fills the air. The floor is rain-wet black concrete that mirrors all the neon in long coloured streaks. Deep blacks, very saturated coloured light on every surface, high contrast, sharp fine detail, cinematic. No people. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no brand names, no characters from real games.
cottage.note: This world's screens are dim grey glass with a second panel under each. find-screens.py ran with level 0.27, top 0.40 and MIN_LAT=2.5, and face-screens.py rebuilt the screens to face the capture point.

gta.prompt: The inside of a large cyberpunk arcade hall at night, seen from the middle of its open floor. The hall is dense and glowing: long rows of retro arcade cabinets with bright blank screens line every wall, their cases edged in hot magenta, electric cyan and amber light. Set into each of the four walls are two tall empty archways framed with thick bright neon tubes, eight archways in all, each opening into darkness. Above, a dark industrial ceiling of exposed pipes, vents and bundled cables carries long magenta and cyan neon strips and hanging lamps. Glowing abstract neon shapes, stripes and arrows hang on the brick and steel walls. The floor is wet black concrete that mirrors every light, with a wide clear circle in the middle. Thin coloured haze in the air. Deep saturated colour, strong contrast, sharp fine detail, cinematic and moody. No people. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no brand names, no characters from real games.
gta.note: The first hall, with cabinets along brick walls and two neon arches. Its cabinets have two panels and stand far from the visitor, so find-screens.py ran with level 0.5 and MIN_LAT=2.5, face-screens.py rebuilt the screens, and the two nearest of them are used.
